subject: radiology
title: Silhouette Sign, Air Bronchogram and Cardiothoracic Ratio

steps.title: Same density plus contact erases borders
steps.tx: **Silhouette sign** is the loss of a normal border when two structures of the same radiographic density touch each other. The heart and consolidated lung are both soft tissue density, so pneumonia against the heart erases that heart border on the frontal film. A lesion separated from the heart by aerated lung keeps the border sharp, placing the lesion in a different lobe or the mediastinum.
steps.say: Silhouette sign is the loss of a normal border when two structures of the same density touch each other. A lesion separated from the heart by aerated lung keeps the border sharp, placing it in a different lobe.

steps.title: Right middle lobe erases right heart border
steps.tx: **Right middle lobe** consolidation touches the right atrial border, so its pneumonia wipes out the right heart edge while the right diaphragm stays visible. Left lower lobe consolidation instead erases the left hemidiaphragm outline and leaves the heart border intact. Lingular consolidation erases the left heart border. Matching the erased border to the structure it touches names the lobe without a lateral film.
steps.say: Right middle lobe consolidation touches the right atrial border, so its pneumonia wipes out the right heart edge while the diaphragm stays visible. Left lower lobe consolidation erases the diaphragm outline instead. Lingular consolidation erases the left heart border. Matching the erased border to the structure it touches names the lobe.

steps.title: Diaphragm domes and the lateral film
steps.tx: **Hemidiaphragm silhouette** also separates left from right on the lateral view. The heart touches the left hemidiaphragm and stops its outline short of the front, while the right dome is traced fully from front to back. The stomach bubble sits directly under the left dome, and the right dome peak usually rides higher. These three checks rescue laterality when markers are missing.

steps.title: Hilum overlay sign
steps.tx: **Hilum overlay sign** applies the same density logic at the hilum. If hilar vessels vanish inside a mass shadow, the mass touches them and sits in the hilum itself. If vessels stay visible through the shadow, the mass lies in front of or behind the hilum, most often in the anterior mediastinum or descending aorta. One frontal film then sorts the compartment before cross sectional imaging.

steps.title: Air bronchogram
steps.tx: **Air bronchogram** shows dark branching airways inside white consolidated lung because alveoli around them have filled with fluid, pus or cells while bronchi stay air filled. It proves the opacity is intrapulmonary airspace disease rather than a pleural collection, which pushes bronchi aside instead of outlining them. Absence of an air bronchogram in a complete lobe opacity favours obstructive collapse with a blocked bronchus.

steps.title: Cardiothoracic ratio
steps.tx: **Cardiothoracic ratio** divides the widest cardiac diameter by the widest internal chest diameter on an erect posteroanterior film. Above 0.5 in an adult means cardiomegaly, with 15.5 cm as a rough absolute upper heart width. An anteroposterior supine film magnifies the heart and fakes enlargement, so the ratio is only trusted on a well inspired erect posteroanterior view with the scapulae rotated out.
steps.say: Cardiothoracic ratio divides the widest cardiac diameter by the widest internal chest diameter on an erect posteroanterior film. Above zero point five in an adult means an enlarged heart. A supine anteroposterior film magnifies the heart and fakes enlargement, so the ratio is trusted only on a well inspired erect view.

steps.title: Cervicothoracic sign
steps.tx: **Cervicothoracic sign** uses the clavicles to place a mediastinal mass. The anterior mediastinum ends at the clavicles, so a mass whose outline survives above the clavicles must sit behind, in the posterior mediastinum or neck. A thyroid goitre sinking into the chest keeps a visible upper border above the clavicles for exactly this reason, separating it from an anterior mediastinal tumour whose top fades at the clavicles.

steps.title: Collapse shifts structures toward it
steps.tx: **Lobar collapse** loses volume, so the trachea, mediastinum and diaphragm shift toward the white lobe, the opposite pattern to a large effusion pushing them away. The pictured comparison pairs consolidation, which keeps volume and outlines bronchi, with collapse pulling fissures and hilum out of place. Raised hemidiaphragm, rib crowding and compensatory overinflation of the remaining lung complete the collapse checklist.
